gadgets.sink: `path -i -m beg` does not decode or normalise, and a bare 101 puts the connection in tunnel mode
gadgets.payload: mirror a bare `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols` with no Upgrade/Connection header
gadgets.effect: tunnel mode, then an arbitrary protocol (e.g. gopher to a backend datastore) over the same socket
gadgets.precondition: a backend whose status line you can influence
gadgets.trap: if the 101 carries Upgrade/Connection, Node's client raises 'upgrade' instead of 'response' and the request hangs to the render timeout

gadgets.versions: 2.8.1 and 2.8.3 (2.8.1 source-confirmed and reproduced offline against haproxy:2.8.1-alpine on 2026-09-26; 2.8.3 confirmed on 2026-09-27 from the No Threshold handout, where `acl is_auth_verify_2fa path_beg,url_dec /auth/verify-2fa` guards a rate limit that //auth/verify-2fa walks straight past)
gadgets.sink: a CONVERTER appended to a path_beg shorthand silently drops its implicit -m beg, degrading a prefix deny to an exact-path deny
gadgets.payload: against  http-request deny if { path_beg,url_dec -i /api/v1/get_ticket }  every one of these is ALLOWED: /api/v1/get_ticket/  /api/v1/get_ticket/x  /api/v1/./get_ticket  //api/v1/get_ticket  (curl --path-as-is)
gadgets.effect: the rule reads as a prefix deny and behaves as an exact string match. Two-config differential on 2.8.1: WITH ',url_dec' the trailing-slash and suffix forms return 200; with the converter removed they return 403. Separately, and independently of the converter bug, HAProxy resolves no dot segments and no leading double slash, so /api/v1/./get_ticket and //api/v1/get_ticket reach a normalising backend (Werkzeug) in BOTH configs.
gadgets.precondition: the denial is HAProxy's own HTML page rather than the app's error format -- that is what identifies the proxy as the denier
gadgets.trap: curl collapses ./ client-side unless --path-as-is is passed, so the bypass silently fails to fire and looks like a dead end. url_dec buys nothing here: /api/v1/%2e/get_ticket is allowed either way, since the decoded /api/v1/./get_ticket does not begin with the blocked prefix either, and Werkzeug does not percent-decode before route matching so it 404s. /api/v1//get_ticket answers 308 (Werkzeug merges the slash and redirects), not 200. The query string is not part of the path sample, so ?x=1 is still denied. A hardening converter added to a *_beg / *_end / *_sub rule is a REGRESSION on this version -- always re-measure the match method after adding one.

gadgets.versions: 2.8.3 (config read from the handout, behaviour measured live, 2026-09-27)
gadgets.sink: a stick-table rate limit has TWO keys, and both are usually attackable: the ACL that decides WHETHER to track, and the expression the counter is bucketed BY
gadgets.payload:
given
  acl is_x path_beg,url_dec /auth/verify-2fa
  http-request track-sc0 hdr(X-Forwarded-For) if is_x
  http-request deny deny_status 429 if is_x { sc_http_req_rate(0) gt 20 }
either  //auth/verify-2fa  (the ACL never matches, so nothing is tracked)  or  a different X-Forwarded-For on every request  (each lands in its own bucket)
gadgets.effect: a four-digit second factor that is unbruteforceable through the front door falls in a few hundred requests. Measured as four concurrent 40-request bursts against one live instance: exact path with no header 20x400 then 14x429; exact path with a rotating header 40x400 and no 429; a second no-header burst 38x429, proving the bucket was still hot when the rotating run passed; doubled slash 39x400.
gadgets.precondition: for the header route, the config must supply the header only when it is missing -- `http-request add-header X-Forwarded-For %[src] if !{ req.hdr(X-Forwarded-For) -m found }` hands the key to the client. For the path route, the backend must normalise the leading double slash; Werkzeug does.
gadgets.trap: measure with a CONCURRENT burst and keep a no-bypass control in the same run. Fired serially, 30 requests never filled the 60s sliding window and even the control produced no 429, which would have credited the bypass with an effect it had not been shown to have. Also: escaping the ACL escapes every rule guarded by it, including any X-Forwarded-For validity check, so the two routes are not equivalent -- the header route still has to satisfy the IPv4 regex (a malformed value answers 400) while the path route bypasses that too. And note the asymmetry with a plain deny: /auth//login (double slash in the MIDDLE) answers 308 because Werkzeug merges it, so only the LEADING double slash is a bypass.
